newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire opposes refugee aid distribution on its soil.
newsitem.headline: Zaire opposes refugee aid distribution on its soil.

text.p: Zaire said on Wednesday it was asking aid agencies not to use its soil to distribute food for more than a million stranded refugees from Rwanda and Burundi.
Government spokesman Boguo Makeli said aid distribution should be done inside the two neighbouring countries Zaire accuses of aggression, to encourage refugees to go home.

"We are asking humanitarian organisations to stop distributing any aid to the refugees on Zairean soil. They must instead distribute aid in Rwanda and Burundi so that the refugees vcan receive it, having travelled along the humanitarian corridors that have been discussed," Boguo said.

France and Spain have proposed sending an international force to open up humanitarian corridors for the refugees dispersed from camps by two weeks of fighting between the Zaire army and ethnic Tutsis.

Zaire accuses its eastern neighbours of backing the rebels. It boycotted a summit of seven regional leaders in Kenya on Tuesday which urged the United Nations to arrange a "neutral" force to come to the rescue of refugees.
Boguo made no direct comment on the Nairobi summit, which decided on a first step of identifying "sites for temporary sanctuaries", followed by the deployment of a neutral force.
He challenged Rwanda to make good its promise of welcoming the 1.1 million Hutus who fear reprisals for the massacre of up to a million Tutsis in 1994. Tutsis now rule Rwanda.

"The Rwandan regime has said it will accept the return of the refugees. We hope this time they are sincere and that their declaration will be followed by concrete actions," said Boguo, who is Zaire's information minister.
Rwandan Foreign Minister Anastase Gasana said on Tuesday Rwanda would strongly oppose any international military intervention in eastern Zaire but would welcome the Hutus.

"We wish that in spite of everything (the refugees) return to Rwanda. The Rwandan government is ready to do everything to facilitate the return of the refugees," Gasana told a news conference in Brussels.
Aid agencies say they have no precise idea of where the refugees are since fighting forced them to flee camps in eastern Zaire and aid workers looking after them.
